A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BeSimulator and the same core BTSIMBENCH evaluation. Their text, equations, tables and figures are readable and support comparison. v1 ends with references and has no appendices; v2 includes readable Appendices A–D.

before.justification: v1 reports original BTSIMBENCH experiments across four LLMs in Table I and component ablations in Table II.

after.justification: v2 reports original comparative experiments and ablations in Tables 3–4, component accuracy results in Appendix C, and a failure case in Appendix D.

M1.justification: Both retain case generation, the world states manager, four-phase CBS, numerical code execution, reflective feedback and BPS evaluation. Action and condition nodes retain their four-phase and two-phase procedures. Renaming Bad Logic to Counterfactuals and supplying more explicit descriptions and prompts do not establish a changed simulation algorithm.

E1.justification: Both evaluate BTSIMBENCH with 75 behavior trees derived from 25 BEHAVIOR-1K tasks, covering good, logically defective and unreachable solutions. The renamed Counterfactuals category matches Bad Logic. Appendix B documents existing tasks, and the new diagnostic analyses remain within the retained benchmark.

E2.justification: v1 compares against few-shot CoT prompting. v2 retains that comparator and adds Best of N with LLM Judge for each backbone in Table 3, selecting among three CoT-generated answers. This is a limited extension of the comparison methods.

E3.justification: DeepSeek-V2-Chat is replaced by DeepSeek-V3 in the main experiments and ablations. Added evaluations introduce three-candidate selection for BoN and separate accuracy metrics for precondition extraction and world-state updating. The benchmark size, main delivery/accuracy metrics and five-feedback limit remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The three existing mechanism ablations remain, while Appendix C adds quantitative analysis separating precondition extraction from state updating. Appendix D adds a traced GetDrink failure in which an incorrect state transition causes rejection of a Good tree. These additions substantially expand the analysis of where simulation fails.

E5.justification: v1 reports point estimates without repeated-run counts or uncertainty. v2 Table 3 explicitly reports five repeated experiments and per-category means with standard deviations. This introduces substantial uncertainty reporting, although it does not establish an increase from a known earlier run count.

E6.justification: The main and ablation results are revised, and BoN and component-accuracy results are added. For example, Claude-based BeSimulator averages are 93.3% in v1 Table I and 92.80% in v2 Table 3. v2's five-run summaries and replacement DeepSeek-V3 experiments should not be interpreted as same-setting performance changes. Table 5 newly shows higher state-update than precondition-extraction accuracy across all four models.

T1.justification: Section III in v1 and Section 3 in v2 retain the same planning quintuple, state-transition formulation and goal condition in Equation 1. No new theorem, proof or substantive mathematical derivation appears in the later appendices.

C1.justification: The central BeSimulator, CBS and BTSIMBENCH contributions remain. However, v2's abstract and introduction explicitly frame the system as preliminary logic validation before conventional simulation, and the separate contribution claiming to introduce behavior simulation is dropped. This refines the intended role without replacing the main contribution.

C2.justification: New Section 7 explicitly acknowledges that FSMs and HTNs were not evaluated and that conventional simulators remain essential for physical fidelity and visual information. Appendices C–D add substantive explanations involving missing, redundant or incorrect preconditions and faulty state transitions. These considerably qualify the earlier reliability and generalization discussion.

D1.justification: v2 adds CBS prompt templates, JSON fields and Python-output conventions in Appendix A, detailed task/node descriptions and XML behavior trees in Appendix B, and a code/data repository pointer in the abstract. These substantially expand reproducibility information beyond v1's procedural descriptions and py_trees link.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion or citations for Reflect, Matsuo et al.'s world-model review, DKPrompt and BEHAVIOR Robot Suite, and replaces the DeepSeek-V2 reference with DeepSeek-V3. Some background references, including GPT-4 and Claude-3, are removed. The three related-work themes remain, with clearer positioning alongside conventional simulators.

P1.justification: Existing introduction, method and experimental paragraphs are extensively rewritten, contributions and baseline descriptions are reorganized, and Bad Logic becomes Counterfactuals. Dedicated limitations and ethics sections and organized appendices expand the document structure. The changes extend well beyond copyediting or inserting new results.

P2.justification: v2 adds a workflow figure, substantially redraws the architecture diagram, reorganizes the main comparison table by backbone, and adds explanatory, diagnostic and appendix tables plus a failure-tree figure. Earlier benchmark illustrations are retained as Figures 3–4. Typography and page layout also change substantially.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves transparency and assessment of reliability: Table 3 adds repeated-run uncertainty and another comparator, Appendices A–B disclose implementation and benchmark details, and Appendices C–D diagnose failures. Section 7 also makes applicability limits explicit. These address important reporting and reproducibility gaps in v1. Evaluation remains confined to behavior trees, and efficiency claims still lack direct timing evidence, but the overall quality gains are substantial.
